doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Gordon Edwards singing 'Love of Mine'
summary: Rowe recalls Edwards's vocal on Love of Mine; Parker remembers hearing him sing a whole tune, and mentions John Montegna and Richard Tee singing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I’m glad you mentioned Gordon Edwards because this morning, actually just before I started this session with you I got up that tune “Love of Mine” — I almost had tears in my eyes. It’s so perfect in every regard and just the way he sang it. And then he gets to the end and if people listen to this there’s this hook and he’s going, “Woman of mine/friend of mine” and then at the end he goes, “stuff of mine.”
Do you remember that moment specifically?

Absolutely. I had only heard him sing you know a bar here and a bar there. I never heard him sing a whole tune like that. Sometimes on stage he would say you know the first line of the song, but he never actually sang like that. So on that session, to hear him sing full throated and that husky baritone, it was great. And I love the lyrics and — there’s a bass player around the city named John Montegna who does a version of “Love of Mine” and sings and plays bass. Great bass player. And I heard his version and it brought it all back to me, you know Gordon singing like that. Richard sang too, he sings one called “I Need Somebody to Love” and also very poignant you know. You hear this big guy singing these very sensitive words. I love that.
